title: The Ant and the Grasshopper

sentences.text: All summer the ant carried grain to a dry storeroom.
The grasshopper sat in the sun and played a bright little tune.
Come and rest, he called. There is plenty of time.
The ant shook her head and said winter does not wait.
She kept working, one seed after another, day after day.
When the cold wind came, the grasshopper's belly was empty.
He went to the storeroom and listened to the wind outside.
The ant opened the door, shared a bowl of grain, and said they could store food together next year.
The grasshopper nodded, warm at last, and put his fiddle down.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A fiddle that can only be played in snow
Getting ready for a hard season, and then sharing
An ant who forgets where the grain is kept
A summer day with no work at all

questions.explanation: The ant stores food while the weather is easy. Winter comes, and she shares with the grasshopper. Preparing and helping are the big idea.

questions.prompt: The ant uses a storeroom. What is a storeroom?

choices.text: A song played on a fiddle
A cold wind from the north
A place where supplies are kept
A bowl used only for water

questions.explanation: A storeroom is a place for keeping supplies. The ant carries grain there so there will be food later.

choices.text: The ant carries grain in summer
The cold wind begins to blow
The grasshopper puts his fiddle down

questions.explanation: First the ant works through summer. Then winter comes. At the end, after the shared bowl, the grasshopper puts his fiddle down.

attribution: Inspired by a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original, and the ending is gentler than the older version.
